title: Accusative 8: Putting It All Together
description: Mixed review: every accusative rule in one lesson.
descriptionRussian: Смешанное повторение: все правила винительного падежа.
intro: Everything from the last seven lessons at once, unlabeled, the way a real sentence hands it to you. The whole case comes down to one question asked before you speak: is this word one of the two kinds that change, or one of the many that do not? Answer that and the right ending follows without effort.
rules: Masculine inanimate: NO change in the accusative (стол → стол, фильм → фильм).
Feminine -а / -я: ending changes to -у / -ю (книга → книгу, песня → песню).
Neuter -о / -е: NO change (письмо → письмо, море → море).
Inanimate plural: NO change (книги → книги, окна → окна).
Masculine animate: ADDS -а (студент → студента, брат → брата).
Pronouns have special accusative forms: я → меня, ты → тебя, он → его, она → её, мы → нас, вы → вас, они → их.
examples: Маша читает журнал. (Masha reads a magazine.) Masculine inanimate, no change.
Антон любит музыку. (Anton loves music.) Feminine -а becomes -у.
Я читаю письмо. (I am reading a letter.) Neuter, no change.
Мы любим книги. (We love books.) Inanimate plural, no change.
Я знаю студента. (I know the student.) Masculine animate adds -а.
Лена видит меня. (Lena sees me.) Pronoun, special form.
Мы любим её. (We love her.) Pronoun, special form.

tables.title: Every Accusative Rule at a Glance

rows.label: Pronouns
cells: меня / тебя / его / её / нас / вас / их

items.hint: Quick check: is журнал a thing or a person? What gender?
items.explanation: Step one: identify the type. Журнал is a thing (inanimate) and masculine. Step two: apply the rule. Masculine inanimate does not change in the accusative.

items.hint: Музыка ends in -а. Which rule does that trigger?
items.explanation: Switch gears: this one is feminine, not masculine. Feminine -а consistently swaps to -у. So музыка → музыку.

items.hint: Студент is a person. What does that change about the rule?
items.explanation: Person, not thing, so the rule shifts. Masculine animate adds -а: студент → студента. Notice that -а plays two different roles in Russian: it is the dictionary ending on feminine nouns (which then change to -у), and it is the added ending on masculine animate nouns.

items.hint: Молоко ends in -о. What gender, and what's the rule?
items.explanation: Молоко is neuter (-о ending) and inanimate. Neuter inanimate joins the same 'no change' club as masculine inanimate.

items.hint: Pronouns don't follow noun rules. What is the accusative of я?
items.explanation: Pronouns are their own system. Я → меня. You can't derive it from gender or animacy rules; it's a memorized form, just like 'me' in English.

items.hint: Ручка ends in -а. Apply the feminine rule.
items.explanation: Notice the pattern: any feminine noun ending in -а behaves the same way. Книга → книгу, музыка → музыку, ручка → ручку. One rule, applied everywhere.

items.hint: Is чай a thing or a person? What gender?
items.explanation: Чай is masculine and a thing, so it falls under the very first rule of the track: no change. Drinks like чай and сок stay in their dictionary form when they are direct objects.

items.hint: Цветы is already plural. Are flowers things or people?
items.explanation: Цветы is the inanimate plural. Like other inanimate plurals, it doesn't change in the accusative: Маша покупает цветы.

items.promptEnglish: I see a table in the room.
items.hint: Стол is masculine inanimate. Does the form change?
items.explanation: Masculine INANIMATE nouns do not change in the accusative: я вижу стол.

items.promptEnglish: Anton has known Ivan since childhood.
items.hint: Иван is a person. What does masculine animate do in the accusative?
items.explanation: Иван is a person, so the accusative borrows the genitive -а: Антон знает Ивана. Compare the inanimate стол, which stays unchanged. Animacy decides which pattern fires.

items.hint: What is the accusative pronoun for она?
items.explanation: Она becomes её as a direct object: мы любим её. Pronouns have their own memorized accusative forms.

items.promptEnglish: I am reading a letter from mom.
items.hint: Письмо ends in -о. What gender, and what is the rule?
items.explanation: Письмо is neuter, and neuter inanimate nouns are identical in the nominative and accusative: я читаю письмо.

items.hint: Books are inanimate. Does the plural change in the accusative?
items.explanation: Inanimate plurals are identical in the nominative and accusative: Маша любит книги.

fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Брат is a person (animate) and masculine. Masculine animate adds -а in the accusative: брат → брата.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я знаю врач в этой больнице.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I know a doctor at this hospital.
errorCorrection.explanation: Врач is a person (animate) and masculine. Masculine animate nouns add -а in the accusative: врач → врача. The bare врач is the nominative form, used only when the doctor is the subject.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha reads a book after dinner.
errorCorrection.explanation: Книга is feminine ending in -а, so the accusative swaps -а → -у: книгу. Книга is the nominative, used only when the book is the subject. The -а → -у rule applies to every feminine noun ending in -а.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша любит он, но не говорит ему об этом.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha loves him but doesn't tell him about it.
errorCorrection.explanation: Pronouns have their own accusative forms. Он is the nominative, used only when 'he' is the subject; as a direct object it becomes его: Маша любит его.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я очень люблю фильмов о Москве.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I really love films about Moscow.
errorCorrection.explanation: Фильмы is an inanimate plural, so the accusative is identical to the nominative plural: фильмы. Фильмов is the genitive plural, used in counting ('много фильмов'); after люблю an inanimate plural stays in its nominative shape.

errorCorrection.sentence: Мама готовит мяса на ужин для всех гостей.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Mom is cooking meat for dinner for all the guests.
errorCorrection.explanation: Мясо is neuter (-о ending) and inanimate. Neuter inanimate accusative is identical to the nominative: мясо. Мяса is the genitive, used in partitive phrases like 'хочу немного мяса' ('I want a bit of meat') but not as a full direct object. For a direct object of готовить, the standard accusative is мясо.

reviewVocab.definition: accusative case (the case of the direct object)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении 'Я вижу маму' слово 'маму' стоит в винительном падеже.

reviewVocab.definition: inanimate (a thing, not a person or animal)
